title: Attention-Density Phase Fusion Scheduler for tenant-aware latency & cost
creator: Aarav Patel
description:
Goal: reduce p95/p99 client-visible latency and per-token cost for mixed workloads by dynamically fusing adjacent phases (prefill + early decode or cross-request decode bursts) when attention-density and kernel-cost models indicate net benefit. We aim to make phase fusion tenant-aware so that tenants with tight latency budgets are protected while opportunistic consolidation reduces tail amplification for bursty workloads.

Problem context: Our current prefills/decodes are split rigidly by request lifecycle which causes kernel underutilization (many small kernel launches) and worse throughput under high concurrency. Existing schedulers either prioritize strict phase isolation (good for per-request latency) or aggressive batching (good for throughput) with poor tenant fairness. We need a middle ground that uses a light-weight attention-density predictor and kernel cost amortization model to decide when to fuse phases, and a tenant credit/latency-budget system to bound regressions.

High-level approach:
1) Attention-density estimator: during prefill we compute a tiny attention-density sketch (per-layer sample of key/query sparsity and average attention mass) plus sequence-length and kv-cache size. The estimator is microsecond-cost and adds <0.5% CPU overhead on the worker.
2) Kernel-cost model: offline-calibrated and periodically updated model that predicts kernel launch time and per-token time for candidate kernels (FP16, int8, fused-attn vs multi-step). The model takes attention-density, seq_len, batch_shape, and active kern cache hit rates.
3) Fusion decision: a cost-benefit comparator that estimates delta in end-to-end latency and token-cost when fusing adjacent phases (or merging small decode windows from multiple tenants). If expected p99 improvement or cost reduction > threshold and no tenant latency budget violations predicted, mark requests for fusion.
4) Tenant-aware constraints: each tenant/request carries a latency budget and a credit score; fusion is allowed only if predicted latency for that request stays within budget or if tenant consents to best-effort consolidation. Credits decay on violations; high-priority tenants can be pinned to no-fusion.
5) Hedge microbatching: when fusion would benefit aggregated throughput but risk a tail for a few requests, issue hedged fast-path fallbacks (speculative partial decode) to ensure latency SLOs.

Expected benefits: lower kernel launch overheads, higher utilization of specialized fused-attn kernels, fewer small microbatches, reduced per-token cost for heavy tail workloads, and improved p95/p99 under mixed tenancy.

Risks and trade-offs: some requests may see small latency regression when fused; incorrect attention-density estimation could lead to suboptimal kernel selection; complexity increases in scheduler and observability. We mitigate these through conservative rollouts, simulation harnesses, and a runtime kill-switch per tenant.
acceptance_criteria: Simulation harness shows >=10% reduction in average kernel launches per 1k requests for mixed small/medium prompt workloads
Canary on prod reduces p99 latency for test tenants by >=8% without increasing p50 by >5%
Per-tenant latency budget enforcement blocks fusion for pinned tenants and logs decisions to console
Kernel-cost model integrated and unit-tested; model updated pipeline runs nightly and artifacts archived
Documentation and SDK hooks exist for tenant opt-in/opt-out and observability labels
design_decisions: Use lightweight attention-density sketch sampled at 2 layers (not full-layer stats) to keep estimator cheap
Cost model is separate from scheduler; scheduler queries model via a cached in-memory table to avoid RPCs during hotpath
Fusion is conservative by default: require minimum expected cost savings and explicit tenant budget check
Implement hedged fast-paths as fallback rather than synchronous cancellation to avoid complex rollbacks
Expose per-decision telemetry (why fused/not fused) tied to request trace IDs for offline analysis
implementation_notes: New runtime flag: --enable-attn-fusion (default off in runtime-1.22) for canarying
Add fields to RequestContext: attention_sketch (byte32), tenant_latency_budget_ms (int), fusion_opt_in (bool)
Kernel cost model format: CSV with columns [kernel_name,seq_len_bucket,attn_density_bucket,median_launch_ms,median_per_token_ms] stored in S3 and cached in worker process
Scheduler change: new PhaseFusionEvaluator component invoked at prefill-complete event; returns decision token and optional hedging plan
Sim harness: extend existing prefillsim to replay traces with attention sketches and validate fusion decisions against ground truth kernels
Backward compat: if attention_sketch missing (old clients), scheduler falls back to length-based heuristics
test_plan: Unit tests for attention sketch generation and serialization
Integration tests: fused vs non-fused in gVisor-like local cluster with synthetic traffic patterns
Performance test matrix across model families (GPT-like 7b, LLaMA2-13b, and a sparse-attn variant), quantization modes (fp16, int8), sequence lengths (64, 512, 2048)
Canary rollout plan: enable --enable-attn-fusion for 3 internal tenants for 48 hours with auto-rollback if p99 or error-rate exceed thresholds
A/B experiment measuring token-cost delta and downstream quality/regression for fused scenarios
